He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn Huskies]]. ==Early life and high school career== Bouknight grew up in [[Crown Heights, Brooklyn]] in New York City.{{cite web |last1=Jacobs |first1=Jeff |title=Bouknight checks all the right boxes for Hurley, Huskies |url=https://www.ctpost.com/sports/jeffjacobs/article/Jeff-Jacobs-Bouknight-checks-all-the-right-boxes-13403695.php |website=[[Connecticut Post]] |accessdate=June 21, 2020 |date=November 18, 2018}} He played [[baseball]] for much of his childhood and started playing basketball in middle school.{{cite web |last1=Amore |first1=Dom |title=UConn Men Notebook: James Bouknight On Campus This Weekend |url=https://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-sp-uconn-men-recruit-james-bouknight-0915-story.html |website=[[Hartford Courant]] |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=September 14, 2018}} He began his high school career with [[La Salle Academy]] in [[Manhattan|Manhattan, New York]]. As a junior, Bouknight averaged 17.4 points per game, leading his team to the [[2017 New York state high school boys basketball championships#Class B|New York Federation Class B state championship]], and was named tournament [[most valuable player]] (MVP).{{cite web |title=Crown Heights Native James Bouknight Becomes National Name |url=https://connecticut.news12.com/clip/14758448/crown-heights-native-james-bouknight-becomes-national-name |publisher=[[News 12 Networks]] |accessdate=June 22, 2020}} He earned [[Catholic High School Athletic Association]] B Division MVP and [[New York State Sportswriters Association]] Class B Player of the Year accolades.{{cite web |last1=Pietrafesa |first1=Dan |title=Catholic School Leagues Honor Top Basketball Players, Coaches |url=https://www.cny.org/stories/catholic-school-leagues-honor-top-basketball-players-coaches,15190 |website=Catholic New York |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=March 1, 2017}}{{cite web |title=All-state teams in boys B, C and D basketball |url=http://newyorksportswriters.org/blog/2017-04-12-new-york-state-sportswriters-association-boys-basketball-all-state-team.shtml |publisher=[[New York State Sportswriters Association]] |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=April 12, 2017}} After the season, Bouknight reclassified down and transferred to [[MacDuffie School]] in [[Granby, Massachusetts]] to gain more exposure.{{cite web |last1=Cordova |first1=David |title=James Bouknight: MacDuffie Scholar Improves On Offers & Introduces Division I Schools To His Game |url=https://davesjoint.net/2018/09/14/james-bouknight-macduffie-scholar-improves-on-offers-introduces-division-i-schools-to-his-game/ |publisher=Dave's Joint |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=September 14, 2018}} In his reclassified junior season, Bouknight averaged 19.3 points, five rebounds and two assists per game before suffering a season-ending [[Tear of meniscus|torn meniscus]] in his left knee. After recovering, he played for the PSA Cardinals alongside [[Cole Anthony]] on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit. As a senior, Bouknight earned All-[[New England Preparatory School Athletic Council]] AA honors.{{cite web |title=NEPSAC announces All-New England awards |url=https://newenglandrecruitingreport.com/in-the-news/nepsac-announces-all-new-england-awards |publisher=New England Recruiting Report |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=March 16, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== Bouknight was a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and was considered the 53rd-best player in the 2019 class by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]]. On September 18, 2018, before his senior season, he committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]].{{cite web |last1=Finkelstein |first1=Adam |title=Guard James Bouknight commits to UConn |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/24722725/guard-james-bouknight-commits-connecticut-huskies |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=September 18, 2018}} Bouknight chose the Huskies over offers from [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]], [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]], [[Temple Owls men's basketball|Temple]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] and [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]], among others.{{cite web |title=James Bouknight |url=https://uconnhuskies.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/james-bouknight/10578 |publisher=University of Connecticut Athletics |accessdate=June 22, 2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = James Bouknight | position = [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = [[Brooklyn|Brooklyn, NY]] | highschool = [[MacDuffie School]] (MA) | feet = 6 | inches = 4 | weight = 180 | 40 = | commitdate = September 18, 2018 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | espn grade = 86 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2019 | rivals ref title = UConn 2019 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2019 UConn Huskies Recruiting Class | rivals school = connecticut | scout s = | espn schoolid = 41 | 247 overall = 53 | rivals overall = 84 | espn overall = 69 | accessdate = October 21, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== On November 7, 2019, Bouknight was suspended for three games by UConn for allegedly fleeing a car crash on September 27. He had been charged with evading responsibility, interfering with a police officer, traveling too fast for conditions and operating a motor vehicle without a license.{{cite web |title=UConn's James Bouknight suspended 3 games after car crash |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28030241/uconn-james-bouknight-suspended-3-games-car-crash |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=November 7, 2019}} On February 9, 2020, Bouknight scored a freshman season-high 23 points in a 72–71 overtime win over [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]]. He scored 19 points in the second half and overtime and made the two game-sealing free throws.{{cite web |last1=Amore |first1=Dom |title=James Bouknight becomes the go-to difference-maker and more takeaways from UConn's win over Cincinnati |url=https://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-sp-clb-uconn-men-folo-takeaways-cincinnati-20200211-20200210-uowvuz5tf5aw5dkgepopmmlgn4-story.html |website=[[Hartford Courant]] |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=February 10, 2020}} One day later, Bouknight was named [[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) Player of the Week.{{cite web |title=Bouknight Named AAC Player Of The Week |url=https://uconnhuskies.com/news/2020/2/10/mens-basketball-bouknight-named-aac-player-of-the-week.aspx |publisher=University of Connecticut Athletics |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=February 10, 2020}} On February 29, he had his first double-double of 19 points and 10 rebounds in a 84–63 victory over [[East Carolina Pirates men's basketball|East Carolina]].{{cite news |title=Vital scores 27 pts., leads UConn past East Carolina, 84–63 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169494 |accessdate=June 23, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 29, 2020}} As a freshman, he averaged 13 points, 4.1 rebounds and 1.3 assists per game and was a Third Team All-AAC and All-Freshman Team selection.{{cite web |last1=Amore |first1=Dom |title=Christian Vital, James Bouknight represent UConn men on all-AAC teams |url=https://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-sp-clb-uconn-notebook-all-aac-20200311-20200310-ntxlzbpzpng7nf3w3jhmymxe3e-story.html |website=[[Hartford Courant]] |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=March 10, 2020}} At the beginning of his sophomore season, Bouknight was named to the preseason [[John R. Wooden Award]] watch list.{{Cite web|title=Bouknight On Watch List For Wooden Award|url=https://uconnhuskies.com/news/2020/11/30/mens-basketball-bouknight-on-watch-list-for-wooden-award|access-date=2020-12-06|website=University of Connecticut Athletics|language=en}} On December 20, 2020, he scored a career-high 40 points in a 76–74 overtime loss to ninth-ranked [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]].{{cite web |title=Bouknight Explodes for 40, But Huskies Drop Big East Opener In Overtime |url=https://uconnhuskies.com/news/2020/12/20/mens-basketball-bouknights-career-day-not-enough-as-huskies-drop-big-east-opener.aspx |website=University of Connecticut Athletics |access-date=December 21, 2020 |date=December 20, 2020}} On January 5, 2021, he suffered an elbow injury against [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]], and missed eight games after undergoing surgery.{{cite web |last1=Amore |first1=Dom |title=James Bouknight cleared to rejoin UConn men for game against Providence Tuesday |url=https://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-sp-uconn-men-james-bouknight-injury-20210216-20210216-sgjfwlycqbfqfnycgd4d7by4gy-story.html |website=[[Hartford Courant]] |access-date=July 21, 2021 |date=February 16, 2021}} As a sophomore, he averaged 18.7 points and 5.7 rebounds per game, earning First Team All-[[Big East Conference|Big East]] honors. On March 31, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Wojnarowski |first1=Adrian |title=UConn Huskies' James Bouknight entering 2021 NBA draft, will hire agent |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31172084/uconn-huskies-james-bouknight-declare-nba-draft |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 21, 2021 |date=March 31, 2021}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]] | '''28''' || '''16''' || 25.9 || '''.462''' || '''.347''' || '''.822''' || 4.1 || 1.3 || .8 || .2 || 13.0 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]] | 15 || 14 || '''31.7''' || .447 || .293 || .778 || '''5.7''' || '''1.8''' || '''1.1''' || '''.3''' || '''18.7''' |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 43 || 30 || 27.9 || .456 || .320 || .802 || 4.7 || 1.5 || .9 || .2 || 15.0 {{S-end}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://uconnhuskies.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/james-bouknight/11135 UConn Huskies bio] {{Authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Bouknight, James}} [[Category:2000 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from New York City]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Brooklyn]] [[Category:UConn Huskies men's basketball players]]
